blocks.text: Ezekiel 14 contains 23 verses. It opens with: Then came certain of the elders of Israel unto me, and sat before me. It concludes with: And they shall comfort you, when ye see their way and their doings; and ye shall know that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it, saith the Lord Jehovah. Supplied contextual evidence for this passage adds: Ezekiel 14 treats Job as a renowned righteous figure, but that reception does not settle the genre or historical referentiality of the completed book. Job's prose setting, poetic dialogue, literary artistry, and ancient reception must be distinguished rather than used as shortcuts to prove either modern biography or pure fiction.
